claim: Small proteins are typically defined as polypeptides consisting of 50 or fewer amino acids.
source: Typically defined as polypeptides consisting of 50 or fewer amino acids, small proteins originate from the translation of distinct small open reading frames (sORFs), rather than from the cleavage of larger precursor proteins or synthesis via ribosome-independent mechanisms (Hemm et al., 2020; Storz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Small proteins originate from the translation of distinct small open reading frames (sORFs), rather than from the cleavage of larger precursor proteins or synthesis via ribosome-independent mechanisms.
source: Typically defined as polypeptides consisting of 50 or fewer amino acids, small proteins originate from the translation of distinct small open reading frames (sORFs), rather than from the cleavage of larger precursor proteins or synthesis via ribosome-independent mechanisms (Hemm et al., 2020; Storz et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Recent advancements in genome and transcriptome sequencing, ribosome-profiling techniques, proteomics, and bioinformatic analyses have led to the discovery of numerous previously unannotated small proteins in all domains of life.
source: Recent advancements in genome and transcriptome sequencing, ribosome-profiling techniques, proteomics, and bioinformatic analyses have led to the discovery of numerous previously unannotated small proteins in all domains of life and efforts to elucidate the targets and functions of these proteins (Andrews and Rothnagel, 2014; D'Lima et al., 2017; Hemm et al., 2008; Steinberg and Koch, 2021; Su et al., 2013; Weaver et al., 2019; Weidenbach et al., 2022; Yuan et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Bacterial small proteins have been implicated in many fundamental physiological processes, including cell division, sporulation, lysis, transport, stress responses, virulence, antibiotic resistance, and cell-to-cell communication.
source: The detection and characterization of small proteins in bacteria have been a particularly prolific research area over the past decade, and bacterial small proteins have been implicated in many fundamental physiological processes, including cell division, sporulation, lysis, transport, stress responses, virulence, antibiotic resistance, and cell-to-cell communication (for reviews, see Duval and Cossart, 2017; Garai and Blanc-Potard, 2020; Hemm et al., 2020; Storz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: The short lengths of the coding sequences and subsequent lack of conserved protein domains render it challenging to identify small protein orthologs and establish evolutionary relationships between small proteins across different organisms.
source: In addition to the current underannotation of sORFs within genomic databases, the short lengths of the coding sequences and subsequent lack of conserved protein domains render it challenging to identify small protein orthologs and establish evolutionary relationships between small proteins across different organisms.
evidence: This is a statement about the challenges in studying small proteins, based on established knowledge.

claim: Most bacterial small proteins appear to be poorly conserved and are limited to a single species or a few closely related bacteria.
source: Instead, most appear to be poorly conserved and are limited to a single species or a few closely related bacteria (Alix and Blanc-Potard, 2009; Storz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Large-scale expression studies demonstrate pervasive transcription of non-genic stretches within characterized genomes.
source: Large-scale expression studies demonstrate pervasive transcription of non-genic stretches within characterized genomes (Dinger et al., 2008) and ribosome-profiling data indicate that many noncoding RNAs are engaged by the ribosome (Carvunis et al., 2012; Wilson and Masel, 2011), supporting the notion that the expression of randomly occurring sORFs from non-genic sequences can serve as a pool for the de novo selection of beneficial functions (Baek et al., 2017; Hemm et al., 2008; Samayoa et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Ribosome-profiling data indicate that many noncoding RNAs are engaged by the ribosome.
source: Large-scale expression studies demonstrate pervasive transcription of non-genic stretches within characterized genomes (Dinger et al., 2008) and ribosome-profiling data indicate that many noncoding RNAs are engaged by the ribosome (Carvunis et al., 2012; Wilson and Masel, 2011), supporting the notion that the expression of randomly occurring sORFs from non-genic sequences can serve as a pool for the de novo selection of beneficial functions (Baek et al., 2017; Hemm et al., 2008; Samayoa et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Genes recently emerged from noncoding DNA are often short in length, poorly conserved, composed primarily of hydrophobic amino acids, and tend to form alpha-helical domains.
source: Furthermore, several reports show that genes recently emerged from noncoding DNA are often short in length, poorly conserved, composed primarily of hydrophobic amino acids, and tend to form alpha-helical domains – all of which are hallmark characteristics of most small proteins described to date (Carvunis et al., 2012; Storz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: De novo small proteins with beneficial functions can be selected in vivo from completely random DNA sequence libraries.
source: Recent experimental work from our group has demonstrated that de novo small proteins with beneficial functions can be selected in vivo from completely random DNA sequence libraries.
evidence: This is a statement about the authors' prior work.

claim: Previously isolated de novo small proteins confer antibiotic resistance by altering cell permeability via direct interactions with the cell membrane.
source: Specifically, our previously isolated de novo small proteins confer antibiotic resistance by altering cell permeability via direct interactions with the cell membrane (Knopp et al., 2019) or by activating a sensor kinase via protein–protein interactions (Knopp et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Previously isolated de novo small proteins confer antibiotic resistance by activating a sensor kinase via protein–protein interactions.
source: Specifically, our previously isolated de novo small proteins confer antibiotic resistance by altering cell permeability via direct interactions with the cell membrane (Knopp et al., 2019) or by activating a sensor kinase via protein–protein interactions (Knopp et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: An earlier study by Digianantonio and Hecht using structurally constrained and partially randomized DNA libraries showed that selected proteins 102 amino acids in length can rescue an Escherichia coli auxotroph caused by the deletion of serB.
source: Along similar lines, an earlier study by Digianantonio and Hecht using structurally constrained and partially randomized DNA libraries showed that selected proteins 102 amino acids in length can rescue an Escherichia coli auxotroph caused by the deletion of serB (Digianantonio and Hecht, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The dependence of the growth restoration on the deattenuation/increased transcription of the his operon and subsequent upregulation of the multi-copy suppressor, HisB, points toward a possible protein-RNA regulatory interaction as the underlying molecular basis of the rescue.
source: While the precise mechanism of these semi-random proteins has not been elucidated, the dependence of the growth restoration on the deattenuation/increased transcription of the his operon and subsequent upregulation of the multi-copy suppressor, HisB, points toward a possible protein-RNA regulatory interaction as the underlying molecular basis of the rescue.
evidence: This is an inference based on prior research findings.

claim: The authors utilized random sequence expression libraries to select for de novo small proteins that can restore the growth of an auxotrophic E. coli strain lacking the conditionally essential SerB enzyme.
source: To experimentally investigate the extent to which completely random, unconstrained, and/or noncoding sequences can serve as substrates for natural de novo gene evolution, we utilized random sequence expression libraries (Knopp et al., 2019) to select for de novo small proteins that can restore the growth of an auxotrophic E. coli strain lacking the conditionally essential enzyme, SerB, and characterized the mechanisms responsible for the rescue phenotype.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The authors isolated three small proteins from their screen that are less than or equal to 50 amino acids in length.
source: We isolated three small proteins from our screen that are less than or equal to 50 amino acids in length and are novel and distinct from those isolated from past studies.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results.

claim: The selected small proteins are novel and distinct from those isolated from past studies.
source: We isolated three small proteins from our screen that are less than or equal to 50 amino acids in length and are novel and distinct from those isolated from past studies.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results.

claim: The selected proteins confer their rescue effect by upregulating the alternative enzyme HisB.
source: Our selected proteins confer their rescue effect by upregulating the alternative enzyme HisB, and the increase in hisB expression is likely caused by direct RNA-binding interactions with the regulatory 5′ end of the his operon mRNA transcript.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental findings.

claim: The increase in hisB expression is likely caused by direct RNA-binding interactions with the regulatory 5′ end of the his operon mRNA transcript.
source: Our selected proteins confer their rescue effect by upregulating the alternative enzyme HisB, and the increase in hisB expression is likely caused by direct RNA-binding interactions with the regulatory 5′ end of the his operon mRNA transcript.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental findings and interpretation.

claim: The five libraries encode small proteins ranging from 10 to 50 amino acids in length.
source: The five libraries encode small proteins ranging from 10 to 50 amino acids in length (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental materials, supported by Figure 1A.

claim: Three of the libraries (rnd10, rnd20, rnd50a) encode repeats of NNB, where N encodes A, C, G, or T at equal ratios and B encodes only C, G, or T.
source: Three of the libraries (rnd10, rnd20, rnd50a) encode repeats of NNB, where N encodes A, C, G, or T at equal ratios and B encodes only C, G, or T.
evidence: This is a description of the library design.

claim: The NNB restriction was chosen to remove two of the three stop codons to increase the likelihood of obtaining full-length proteins within the sORFs, while maintaining amino acid ratios comparable to that of NNN repeats.
source: This restriction was chosen to remove two of the three stop codons to increase the likelihood of obtaining full-length proteins within the sORFs, while maintaining amino acid ratios comparable to that of NNN repeats.
evidence: This is an explanation of the rationale behind the library design.

claim: Libraries 50b and 50c were biased to encode a higher fraction of primordial and hydrophilic residues.
source: Libraries 50b and 50c were biased to encode a higher fraction of primordial and hydrophilic residues in an effort to recapitulate potential coding sequences in early life (Ring et al., 1972) or generate proteins without a strong hydrophobic core that are structurally flexible (Dunker et al., 2005; Dyson, 2016), respectively.
evidence: This is a description of the library design, supported by citations.

claim: The total diversity of the libraries was approximately 5.8 × 10^8.
source: The total diversity of the libraries was approximately 5.8 × 108.
evidence: This is a quantitative description of the library diversity.

claim: The authors selected 74 KEIO strains for their screen.
source: A previous study showed that 155 KEIO strains are unable to grow on M9 minimal medium (Baba et al., 2006; Joyce et al., 2006; Patrick et al., 2007); we selected 74 of these strains for our screen (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach.

claim: The authors were only able to isolate randomly generated sORFs that could rescue the ΔserB auxotroph from their screens.
source: While multi-copy suppression of these auxotrophies has previously been shown to be common (Patrick et al., 2007), we were only able to isolate randomly generated sORFs that could rescue the ΔserB auxotroph from our screens.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results.

claim: The inserts encoded in the three selected variants cause little to no reduction in fitness when expressed during exponential phase growth in rich medium.
source: The inserts encoded in the three selected variants cause little to no reduction in fitness when expressed during exponential phase growth in rich medium (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and were designated his deattenuating protein(s) 1–3 (Hdp1-Hdp3).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The selected variants were designated his deattenuating protein(s) 1–3 (Hdp1-Hdp3).
source: The inserts encoded in the three selected variants cause little to no reduction in fitness when expressed during exponential phase growth in rich medium (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and were designated his deattenuating protein(s) 1–3 (Hdp1-Hdp3).
evidence: This is a statement of nomenclature.

claim: Hdp1 and Hdp2 variants containing frameshifts and premature stop codons were not able to restore growth of the auxotrophic mutant on minimal medium.
source: To determine whether the rescue of the serB deletion mutant is facilitated by expression of the mRNA or the encoded protein, we constructed Hdp1 and Hdp2 variants containing frameshifts and premature stop codons. None of these constructs were able to restore growth of the auxotrophic mutant on minimal medium, indicating that the translated proteins are responsible for the rescue (Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: The translated proteins are responsible for the rescue.
source: None of these constructs were able to restore growth of the auxotrophic mutant on minimal medium, indicating that the translated proteins are responsible for the rescue (Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Recoded Hdp2 retained function, demonstrating that the rescue is indeed mediated by the translated sORF.
source: Furthermore, we generated variants encoding the proteins using alternative codons, which extensively changes the nucleotide sequence while maintaining the amino acid sequence. Recoded Hdp2 retained function, demonstrating that the rescue is indeed mediated by the translated sORF (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results and interpretation, supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Recoding Hdp1 resulted in a loss of function, likely due to effects on expression levels and mRNA stability.
source: However, recoding Hdp1 resulted in a loss of function, likely due to effects on expression levels and mRNA stability.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results and interpretation.

claim: An Hdp1 variant in which the start codon was removed did not allow growth on minimal medium, confirming that protein expression is essential for rescue.
source: Therefore, to further demonstrate that the functionality of this insert is also dependent on the encoded protein rather than the mRNA transcript, we constructed an additional Hdp1 variant in which the start codon was removed. This variant did not allow growth on minimal medium, confirming that protein expression is essential for rescue (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results and interpretation, supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The encoded small proteins are hydrophobic 49- and 50-mers.
source: The encoded small proteins are hydrophobic 49- and 50-mers (Figure 1C) and truncation experiments showed that 10 amino acids could be removed from the C- and N-terminus of Hdp1 and Hdp2, respectively, with maintained functionality (Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 1C.

claim: Truncation experiments showed that 10 amino acids could be removed from the C- and N-terminus of Hdp1 and Hdp2, respectively, with maintained functionality.
source: The encoded small proteins are hydrophobic 49- and 50-mers (Figure 1C) and truncation experiments showed that 10 amino acids could be removed from the C- and N-terminus of Hdp1 and Hdp2, respectively, with maintained functionality (Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: Multiple sequence alignments using Clustal Omega revealed a putative motif of 10 amino acids that was shared among all three proteins.
source: Multiple sequence alignments using Clustal Omega (Chojnacki et al., 2017) revealed a putative motif of 10 amino acids that was shared among all three proteins (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a statement of the computational analysis results, supported by Figure 1D.

claim: This possible motif has not been described previously and is not recognized in the Pfam database of protein families.
source: This possible motif has not been described previously and is not recognized in the Pfam database of protein families (El-Gebali et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement based on database searches.

claim: All three isolated proteins are predicted to be mainly alpha-helical with high confidence by AlphaFold as well as JPred4.
source: All three isolated proteins are predicted to be mainly alpha-helical with high confidence by AlphaFold as well as JPred4 (Drozdetskiy et al., 2015; Jumper et al., 2021; Mirdita et al., 2022; Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a statement of the computational prediction results, supported by Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Some loss-of-function mutations observed were clustered in or near the similarity region, suggesting that it may have a role in rescue.
source: To examine the potential functional role of this region of similarity and define other functional regions of the proteins, we performed random mutagenesis of the hdp1 and hdp2 genes and screened for mutant variants that were unable to rescue the ΔserB mutant on minimal medium. Some loss-of-function mutations observed were clustered in or near the similarity region, suggesting that it may have a role in rescue (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3; Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results and interpretation, supported by Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3, and Supplementary file 1b.

claim: SerB is a phosphatase that catalyzes the conversion of 3-phospho-L-serine to L-serine in the final step of L-serine biosynthesis.
source: SerB is a phosphatase that catalyzes the conversion of 3-phospho-L-serine to L-serine in the final step of L-serine biosynthesis (Ravnikar and Somerville, 1987).
evidence: This is a statement of established biochemical knowledge, supported by a citation.

claim: None of the Hdp proteins enabled growth of either a ΔserA or ΔserC mutant on minimal medium.
source: To test whether the isolated proteins can bypass the normal pathway for L-serine biosynthesis, we examined whether they could rescue auxotrophies caused by the deletion of the enzymes upstream in this linear pathway (Figure 1F). On minimal medium, none of the Hdp proteins enabled growth of either a ΔserA or ΔserC mutant, which encode a dehydrogenase and an aminotransferase, respectively, indicating that the Hdps do not re-route the metabolism to synthesize serine via a different pathway, but rather they relieve the need for SerB (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The Hdps do not re-route the metabolism to synthesize serine via a different pathway, but rather they relieve the need for SerB.
source: On minimal medium, none of the Hdp proteins enabled growth of either a ΔserA or ΔserC mutant, which encode a dehydrogenase and an aminotransferase, respectively, indicating that the Hdps do not re-route the metabolism to synthesize serine via a different pathway, but rather they relieve the need for SerB (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: E. coli encodes 23 cytoplasmic haloacid dehydrogenase (HAD)-like hydrolases (including SerB), which share limited sequence similarity but have strongly overlapping substrate specificities.
source: E. coli encodes 23 cytoplasmic haloacid dehydrogenase (HAD)-like hydrolases (including SerB), which share limited sequence similarity but have strongly overlapping substrate specificities (Kuznetsova et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge, supported by a citation.

claim: Besides ΔserB, only ΔhisB exhibited an auxotrophic phenotype.
source: To determine whether expression of the selected small proteins could functionally replace any of the other HAD-like phosphatases, we tested the growth defects of individual HAD-knockout mutants. Besides ΔserB, only ΔhisB exhibited an auxotrophic phenotype.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results.

claim: Only the ΔserB auxotrophic mutant could be rescued by expression of the isolated proteins.
source: However, only the ΔserB auxotrophic mutant could be rescued by expression of the isolated proteins (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 1G.

claim: Past studies showed that the overexpression of two HAD-like phosphatases, HisB and Gph, as well as the nonrelated putative phosphatase YtjC, can rescue ΔserB auxotrophy.
source: Past studies showed that the overexpression of two HAD-like phosphatases, HisB and Gph, as well as the nonrelated putative phosphatase YtjC, can rescue ΔserB auxotrophy (Patrick et al., 2007; Yip and Matsumura, 2013).
evidence: This is a statement of prior research findings, supported by citations.

claim: Removal of YtjC and Gph did not affect the rescue.
source: We therefore tested whether the small protein-mediated rescue is dependent on the presence of any of these three proteins. While removal of YtjC and Gph did not affect the rescue, deletion of hisB abolished the ability of Hdp1-Hdp3 to rescue the ΔserB auxotrophy (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Deletion of hisB abolished the ability of Hdp1-Hdp3 to rescue the ΔserB auxotrophy.
source: While removal of YtjC and Gph did not affect the rescue, deletion of hisB abolished the ability of Hdp1-Hdp3 to rescue the ΔserB auxotrophy (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The Hdps rescue the lack of SerB by upregulating expression of HisB, which can functionally replace SerB and thereby restore L-serine biosynthesis and growth on minimal medium.
source: Based on these findings, we hypothesized that the Hdps rescue the lack of SerB by upregulating expression of HisB, which can functionally replace SerB and thereby restore L-serine biosynthesis and growth on minimal medium (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental results.

claim: A previous study showed that sequence libraries encoding semi-random proteins that fold into predefined four-helix bundles could be used to select proteins that upregulate HisB to rescue SerB deficiency.
source: This is in agreement with the previous Digianantonio and Hecht study, which showed that sequence libraries encoding semi-random proteins that fold into predefined four-helix bundles could be used to select proteins that upregulate HisB to rescue SerB deficiency (Digianantonio and Hecht, 2016; Fisher et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement of prior research findings, supported by citations.

claim: Expression of the his operon is regulated by a transcriptional attenuator located near the 5′ end of the his operon mRNA transcript that responds to levels of charged tRNA^His.
source: Expression of the his operon, consisting of the structural genes hisG, hisD, hisC, hisB, hisH, hisA, hisF, and hisI, is regulated by a transcriptional attenuator located near the 5′ end of the his operon mRNA transcript that responds to levels of charged tRNAHis (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the his operon regulation.

claim: Under histidine-rich conditions, a histidine-rich leader peptide (HisL) is synthesized and a terminator hairpin forms, resulting in transcription termination.
source: Under histidine-rich conditions, a histidine-rich leader peptide (HisL) is synthesized and a terminator hairpin forms, resulting in transcription termination.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the his operon regulation, supported by citations in the figure legend.

claim: Under histidine-poor conditions, the ribosome will stall at the HisL histidine codons due to the lack of charged tRNA^His, and as a result, an anti-terminator hairpin forms that allows continued transcription and subsequent expression of the downstream structural genes.
source: However, under histidine-poor conditions, the ribosome will stall at the HisL histidine codons due to the lack of charged tRNAHis. As a result, an anti-terminator hairpin forms that allows continued transcription and subsequent expression of the downstream structural genes (Artz and Broach, 1975; Blasi and Bruni, 1981; Johnston et al., 1980; Kasai, 1974).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the his operon regulation, supported by citations.

claim: The operon promoter is activated upon induction of the stringent response.
source: Additionally, the operon promoter is activated upon induction of the stringent response, offering various potential targets with which the Hdps could interact.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the his operon regulation.

claim: Hdp1 and Hdp3 expression caused an almost 20-fold increase in β-galactosidase activity of the reporter strain carrying the full-length P_hisL-his_operator-lacZ fusion.
source: Hdp1 and Hdp3 expression caused an almost 20-fold increase in β-galactosidase activity of the reporter strain carrying the full-length PhisL-hisoperator-lacZ fusion (under the control of the native PhisL promoter) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 2B.

claim: Only a twofold increase was observed for Hdp2.
source: Only a twofold increase was observed for Hdp2, consistent with our observations of ΔserB strain growth on minimal medium where cells expressing Hdp1 and Hdp3 grew faster than those expressing Hdp2 (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 1G.

claim: A nonfunctional Hdp1 variant containing a L27Q substitution did not increase the β-galactosidase activity of the P_hisL-his_operator-lacZ fusion reporter strain.
source: Correspondingly, a nonfunctional Hdp1 variant containing a L27Q substitution within the similarity region that was derived from the random mutagenesis screens (i.e., did not rescue the ΔserB mutant on minimal medium) did not increase the β-galactosidase activity of the PhisL-hisoperator-lacZ fusion reporter strain (Figure 2B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 2B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, and Supplementary file 1b.

claim: Hdp1 expression had little impact on the β-galactosidase activity of the P_thrL-thr_operator-lacZ reporter strain.
source: To examine the specificity of the Hdp mechanism of action, we also assayed the β-galactosidase activity of a reporter strain carrying the full-length thr operator sequence transcriptionally fused to the lacZ gene on the chromosome. In E. coli, the thr biosynthetic operon is regulated by an operator region that is similar in length, structure, and mechanism to that of the his operon (Kolter and Yanofsky, 1982). As expected, Hdp1 expression had little impact on the β-galactosidase activity of the PthrL-throperator-lacZ reporter strain (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 2B.

claim: The Hdps rescue serB auxotrophy by increasing hisB expression through altering the regulation of the his operon via the his operator region.
source: Overall, these data confirm that the Hdps rescue serB auxotrophy by increasing hisB expression through altering the regulation of the his operon via the his operator region.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Hdp1 expression did not affect the β-galactosidase activity of a lacZ transcriptional fusion under the control of the rrnB P1 promoter and accompanying regulatory sequence.
source: In addition to the negligible impact Hdp1 expression had on the β-galactosidase activity of the full-length PthrL-throperator-lacZ reporter strain, Hdp1 expression did not affect the β-galactosidase activity of a lacZ transcriptional fusion under the control of the rrnB P1 promoter and accompanying regulatory sequence, which is also regulated by the stringent response (Aseev et al., 2014; Paul et al., 2004; Paul et al., 2005; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The rescue effect of Hdp1 was not affected by the deletion of the stringent response genes relA and dksA in the P_hisL-his_operator-lacZ fusion reporter strain.
source: Moreover, the rescue effect of Hdp1 was not affected by the deletion of the stringent response genes relA and dksA in the PhisL-hisoperator-lacZ fusion reporter strain (Paul et al., 2004; Turnbull et al., 2019; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The abundances of only seven proteins were significantly increased upon expression of Hdp1 and Hdp3, all of which were under the regulation of the his operator.
source: The abundances of only seven proteins were significantly increased upon expression of Hdp1 and Hdp3, all of which were under the regulation of the his operator (i.e., the native his operon and modified lac operon) (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: No significant increase in His or modified Lac protein abundance was detected upon expression of Hdp2.
source: However, we did not detect a significant increase in His or modified Lac protein abundance upon expression of Hdp2.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results.

claim: No significant changes to protein abundance were observed upon expression of the Hdp1 L27Q mutant.
source: Consistent with our β-galactosidase activity data, no significant changes to protein abundance were observed upon expression of the Hdp1 L27Q mutant.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results.

claim: The Hdps do not induce his operon expression through the activation or upregulation of stress response pathways.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the Hdps do not induce his operon expression through the activation or upregulation of stress response pathways and that Hdps have a high specificity in their action and do not cause global alterations in gene expression.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Hdps have a high specificity in their action and do not cause global alterations in gene expression.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the Hdps do not induce his operon expression through the activation or upregulation of stress response pathways and that Hdps have a high specificity in their action and do not cause global alterations in gene expression.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: No increase in β-galactosidase activity was observed upon Hdp1 expression for either reporter strain carrying the P_hisL-lacZ or P_hisB-lacZ transcriptional fusions.
source: To assess whether the Hdps alter HisB expression through direct interactions with either of the two native his operon promoters, we generated lacZ transcriptional fusions (with no his operator regulatory sequence) under the control of the PhisL promoter, which is the primary his operon promoter located upstream of the hisL leader peptide gene, and the PhisB promoter, an internal promoter for the operon located just upstream of the hisB gene (Grisolia et al., 1983). No increase in β-galactosidase activity was observed upon Hdp1 expression for either reporter strain carrying the PhisL-lacZ or PhisB-lacZ transcriptional fusions (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 2D.

claim: Hdp1 was still able to increase the β-galactosidase activity of his_operator-lacZ transcriptional fusions in which the native P_hisL promoter was replaced with either the P_lac promoter or the P_araBAD promoter.
source: However, Hdp1 was still able to increase the β-galactosidase activity of hisoperator-lacZ transcriptional fusions in which the native PhisL promoter was replaced with either the Plac promoter or the ParaBAD promoter (induced upon the addition of IPTG or arabinose, respectively), showing that the Hdp rescue mechanism does not require the native his operon PhisL and PhisB promoters.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results.

claim: The Hdp rescue mechanism does not require the native his operon P_hisL and P_hisB promoters.
source: However, Hdp1 was still able to increase the β-galactosidase activity of hisoperator-lacZ transcriptional fusions in which the native PhisL promoter was replaced with either the Plac promoter or the ParaBAD promoter (induced upon the addition of IPTG or arabinose, respectively), showing that the Hdp rescue mechanism does not require the native his operon PhisL and PhisB promoters.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: No increase in β-galactosidase activity was observed upon Hdp1 expression in strains carrying truncated versions of the his operator fused to lacZ.
source: Finally, no increase in β-galactosidase activity was observed upon Hdp1 expression in strains carrying truncated versions of the his operator fused to lacZ (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 2E.

claim: An Hdp1-mediated increase in β-galactosidase activity was not observed for a full-length P_hisL-his_operator-lacZ reporter strain containing a missense mutation within the hisL leader peptide coding sequence (Q5Stop).
source: An Hdp1-mediated increase in β-galactosidase activity was also not observed for a full-length PhisL-hisoperator-lacZ reporter strain containing a missense mutation within the hisL leader peptide coding sequence (Q5Stop) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental results, supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The Hdps require the complete and fully functional his operator regulatory region, consisting of the full-length and intact hisL gene and transcription attenuator sequence, to exert their rescue effect.
